topic: A person learns their childhood best friend doesn't remember them
text: It's been ages since we last talked, and there I was, so eager to reconnect, to pick up right where we left off. I called them out of the blue, hoping to reminisce about the good old days, to laugh at our silly antics. But when I mentioned a specific memory, a shared joke from our younger years, they paused. Then they said it so softly, "I'm sorry, I don't remember that." It hit me then; all the stories, all the secrets, they were just mine now. I tried to play it cool, suggested catching up over coffee. Maybe some memories will resurface, or maybe we’ll make new ones. I'm not giving up that easily.
